summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, recurrent pulmonary emboli on anticoagulation, chronic microcytic anemia, and costochondritis was admitted for acute worsening of chronic left-sided chest pain. Evaluation revealed no cardiac ischemia, pulmonary embolism, or other acute cardiopulmonary pathology. The chest pain was reproducible on palpation, consistent with musculoskeletal etiology. A urinary tract infection was identified on urinalysis and treated with a single dose of antibiotics. Dyspnea resolved without supplemental oxygen, and the patient remained hemodynamically stable. A posterior neck soft tissue swelling was noted, previously diagnosed as a lipoma, to be followed up outpatient. She was discharged home with continued home medications and instructions to monitor weight and follow up with her primary care provider for ongoing management.
problems: Diverticulosis of colon (without mention of hemorrhage)
